newsitem.title: FINLAND: END OF TAX-FREE SALES TO HURT FINNISH FERRY FIRMS.
newsitem.headline: END OF TAX-FREE SALES TO HURT FINNISH FERRY FIRMS.

text.p: The planned abolishment of duty-free purchases in intra-EU travel would reduce Finnish shipping companies' gross margins to zero, the Helsinki Research Institute for Business Administration (LTT) said.
"The loss in gross margins would equal the current annual gross margins," managing director of LTT Jarmo Granfelt told Reuters by telephone on Friday.
Finnish shipping companies' aggregate gross margin was some 1.2 billion markka in 1995. Shipping companies would have to lift ticket prices to maintain profitability, LTT said.

"Compensating the loss in gross margins at current passenger volumes would mean that ticket prices should be raised 150 percent in order to sustain profitability," Granfelt told a news conference on Thursday.
"But a heavy increase in ticket prices would lead to a drop in passenger volumes," he added.
A decrease in passenger volumes would call for a signifcant reduction of capacity and proportionate payroll cuts, LTT said.
In 1995, passenger ferry traffic employed 5,500 people on ships and 1,700 on land, it said in a study.
"If (ferry) capacity were halved, ship owners would have to reduce staff by 2,500 to 3,000 employees working in traffic between Finland and Sweden," Granfelt said.
The Finnish ship building industry would also suffer indirectly from the discontinuation of the duty free system as most of the car ferries operating from Finland are built here, the study said.
An EU directive agreed by the Council of Ministers in 1991 says duty and tax free purchases in intra-EU travel should be abolished in June 1999.
